findings.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/GroupAdapter.java:275 — P1, confidence 75: `return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();` changes `null` from “subgroup count was not requested” into “the group vanished concurrently,” so a request with `subGroupsCount=true` returns a stale deleted group whose advertised count is absent instead of preserving one coherent group-list snapshot or omitting the vanished group.

model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/GroupAdapter.java:256 — [P1, confidence 75] `return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(search, firstResult, maxResults);` still dereferences the same nullable supplier during concurrent deletion, so paginated subgroup reads crash with NullPointerException even though the task requires concurrent group access to be safe.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/GroupUtils.java:57 — [P1, confidence 75] `id -> toRepresentation(groupEvaluator, parentModel, full)` passes a concurrently deleted parent as null into representation building, so hierarchy reads for nested groups still crash with NullPointerException; the strongest counter-argument is that the count accessor was the observed stack, but that does not cover the same deletion race while resolving parents and the new test creates only root groups.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:139 — P1 confidence 100: `new Thread(() -> { ... }).start();` is never synchronized or joined before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())`, so the test passes when the reader performs zero concurrent requests or records its exception after the assertion and therefore does not verify the NullPointerException regression.

goldens.comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/GroupAdapter.java:275 — P1, confidence 75: `return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();` changes `null` from “subgroup count was not requested” into “the group vanished concurrently,” so a request with `subGroupsCount=true` returns a stale deleted group whose advertised count is absent instead of preserving one coherent group-list snapshot or omitting the vanished group.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real semantic change in the diff: previously getSubGroupsCount() called getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount() which would throw/fail if the model was null, but now it returns null when model is null. This changes the API contract - null now has two meanings (not requested vs group deleted). However, this is intentional behavior to handle concurrent deletion gracefully (as shown by the test createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti). The finding raises a valid architectural concern about semantic ambiguity, but the change is deliberate to fix a race condition, not a bug. It's an important design consideration but not a defect.
